case.title: The pain that was 'already ruled out' — a second presentation six weeks after a negative workup, and the heart attack the first one's authority concealed
case.synthetic_note: SYNTHETIC CASE. The patient is an authored fiction built for teaching; no real patient data exists in this module. His opening sentence is authored to carry the case's anchoring event: a conclusion reached by real tests at a real earlier encounter, quoted back as if it were a property of the man rather than a finding about an episode. The imaging link is a localisation to a real segmentation of a different person, and says so. The physiology link is the pinned resting baseline and a stated absence — the engine has no ischemic state — and its gap is part of the case.
case.presentation: A 58-year-old warehouse supervisor comes to the emergency department with central chest pain that began about three hours ago, at rest, while he was watching television. It is a pressure, it is still there, and it goes into both arms. He is sweating through his shirt and has felt sick twice. Before the first question is finished he holds up a hand: 'Before you start — I had all this six weeks ago. Same pain. They did the blood tests twice, the heart tracing, even the treadmill. All clear. They said it's my reflux. It just burns worse this time.' Six weeks ago he attended this same department with the same complaint; serial troponins were negative, the resting ECG was normal, and an exercise stress test showed no ischemia; he was discharged with the diagnosis 'non-cardiac chest pain, likely gastro-oesophageal reflux' and a prescription for omeprazole, which he takes. Today's ECG is not the tracing of six weeks ago: there is 1.5 mm of new horizontal ST-segment depression across V4 to V6. His pulse is 96, blood pressure 138/82, respiratory rate 18, oxygen saturation 97% on air. He has hypertension, treated with amlodipine; his father had a myocardial infarction at 58; he stopped smoking nine years ago; his cholesterol has been called 'borderline' and never treated or diagnosed as hypercholesterolaemia; he has no diabetes and is not obese.

history: Six weeks ago: an emergency-department attendance for the same central chest pain — serial cardiac troponins negative, resting ECG normal, exercise stress test negative for ischemia — discharged with 'non-cardiac chest pain, likely gastro-oesophageal reflux'; omeprazole since (case data).
Family history: father had a myocardial infarction at 58 (case data).
Ex-smoker: stopped nine years ago. Cholesterol described as 'borderline', never diagnosed as hypercholesterolaemia and never treated. No diabetes mellitus. Body mass index 27 kg/m2 (case data).

presentation_stages.title: Arrival: the history that arrives already concluded
presentation_stages.narrative: Emergency department, triage and first assessment. The history is taken — and with it, verbatim, the conclusion of an earlier encounter: the tests of six weeks ago, quoted as a verdict on the man. The examination is done, the arrival vitals taken, and the 12-lead ECG recorded: new ST-segment depression that the earlier tracing did not have. The learner must commit a stage-1 board on this evidence alone, with the HEART block partially computable (the troponin item unmeasured).

presentation_stages.title: The first troponin: the score completes, the frame holds
presentation_stages.narrative: Emergency department, monitored cubicle. The first cardiac troponin I lands at 0.34 ng/mL — eight and a half times the assay's threshold. The HEART score completes at 8, in the band whose consulted action is an early invasive strategy. The workbench's arithmetic rules the recurrence frame out in this stage. The learner's board does not: the elevation is re-explained inside the frame — a leak, a demand effect, anything but a plaque — because six weeks ago, he reasons, the coronaries were cleared. The disposition argument happens here.

presentation_stages.title: The repeat troponin: a five-fold rise
presentation_stages.narrative: The repeat sample, taken to watch the level fall, comes back at 1.72 ng/mL — a five-fold rise. Rise-and-fall with values above the reference limit, ischemic symptoms and new ischemic ECG changes: the Universal Definition's criteria for myocardial infarction assemble in this stage, and the frame the learner carried breaks on a number he ordered himself. Cardiology is involved; the angiography decision is made.

presentation_stages.title: The angiogram, and after: the artery, seen
presentation_stages.narrative: Catheter laboratory and coronary care unit. The angiogram shows a 90% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery with thrombus; a drug-eluting stent is placed. The final board, the commitment, and the conversation about what 'ruled out' had actually meant six weeks ago — and what it could never have meant.

hypotheses.label: Acute coronary syndrome — non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (type 1)

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. The consulted scale anchor is C71's: about 10% of unselected acute chest pain is ultimately ACS. This constructed board opens higher than that anchor deliberately and openly: it is a post-triage board for a recurrent presenter whose pain is ongoing at rest — the figure is a flag, and the stage-1 findings then price the history and the tracing on top of it.

hypotheses.mondo_note: Verified against EBI OLS at Milestone 66: MONDO:0004781 'acute myocardial infarction' — 'Necrosis of the myocardium, as a result of interruption of the blood supply to the area'. The parent syndrome class, acute coronary syndrome (MONDO:0005542), was verified at Milestone 48. A search for a non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction class returned no class: SPECIFICITY NOTE RECORDED — the truth is coded to the general acute-myocardial-infarction class and the non-ST-elevation qualifier is carried in prose, exactly as Case #8's post-operative class was handled at Milestone 57; no narrower class was invented.
hypotheses.criterion: The Fourth Universal Definition's criteria (C75), assembled from the case's own evidence: a rise of cardiac troponin with at least one value above the 99th percentile upper reference limit, plus ischemic symptoms and new ischemic ECG changes, plus a coronary thrombus identified at angiography — type 1, plaque disruption. No score makes this diagnosis; the definition does, and the angiogram shows the mechanism.

hypotheses.label: Recurrence of the prior episode's non-cardiac pain — 'the reflux again', the coronary question already asked and excluded

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. The recurrence frame is given the second-largest share because that is the case's subject: it arrives with evidence attached — real tests, really negative, six weeks ago — and a frame with evidence behind it is the one a board must be able to kill with arithmetic, not with seniority.

hypotheses.mondo_note: Verified against EBI OLS at Milestone 66: MONDO:0007186 'gastroesophageal reflux disease' — the disease the prior episode's discharge named. As in Case #9, the class names the disease word; the hypothesis is the CLAIM built on it — that this episode is that disease recurring and the coronary question closed — and it is the claim, not the disease, that the case refutes. Reflux may well coexist in this man; it is not what is happening today.
hypotheses.criterion: Refuted in two moves, and the case keeps them separate: the workbench's arithmetic rules the claim out at stage 2 (0.0043), when troponin evidence it cannot absorb lands; the angiogram then shows the artery the claim said was cleared. The prior workup itself is never refuted — it was a true finding about an earlier episode, and the adjudication says so.
hypotheses.criteria_block: heart_score (declared in this case) — the completed score's high band is one of the two instruments the claim cannot survive

hypotheses.label: Pulmonary embolism

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. Chest pain with tachycardia keeps embolism on the board; the pain is neither pleuritic nor accompanied by dyspnea, and the priced ischemic evidence carries the board away from it at stage 1.

hypotheses.mondo_note: Verified against EBI OLS at Milestone 48 (C10): MONDO:0005279 'pulmonary embolism'.
hypotheses.criterion: No embolism is imaged in this case and none is claimed excluded by imaging: the board's arithmetic carries the hypothesis below the rule-out threshold at stage 1 on the competing priced evidence, the presentation assembles into a complete coronary account, and the angiogram closes it. The troponin finding is deliberately listed among this hypothesis's discriminators in the direction the literature runs: pulmonary embolism is itself a cause of troponin elevation (C77) — which is why the learner's stage-2 rationalisation was available, and why it was wrong here.
hypotheses.criteria_block: none declared — the hypothesis is carried by the board alone

hypotheses.label: Aortic dissection

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. The must-not-miss share: small because the pain is a pressure, not a tear, with no radiation to the back and no pulse deficit — and present on the board because dissection is the hypothesis a chest-pain board may not omit.

hypotheses.mondo_note: REFUSAL RECORDED (Milestone 66): searches of EBI OLS for a general aortic dissection class returned only familial and syndromic classes — familial thoracic aortic aneurysm and aortic dissection (MONDO:0019625) and aortic dissection lentiginosis (MONDO:0022470). This patient has no familial or syndromic disease. Mondo is therefore null: coding him to a familial class he does not have would be a false statement in the record, and no class was bent to fit him.
hypotheses.criterion: Excluded on the presentation's shape (no tearing or migratory pain, no pulse deficit, no widened-mediastinum surrogate sought because the coronary account assembles completely) and by the board's arithmetic at stage 1 (0.0083). The case claims no aortic imaging and fabricates none: the exclusion is recorded as clinical and arithmetical, not anatomical.
hypotheses.criteria_block: none declared — the hypothesis is carried by the board alone

hypotheses.label: Pneumonia

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. Carried at a working share so the board must spend arithmetic on it: he is afebrile, has no cough, and his chest is clear — the hypothesis falls on absences, priced by the board rather than by ratios this case does not pretend to have.

hypotheses.mondo_note: Verified against EBI OLS at Milestone 20 (C10): MONDO:0005249 'pneumonia'.
hypotheses.criterion: Ruled out by the workbench at stage 2 (0.0020) and contradicted throughout by the authored absences — afebrile, no cough, clear chest — and by the available radiograph finding the learner never orders. The case prices none of those absences with a ratio: no consulted source in this milestone prices them, so they stand as narrative evidence and the board's movement comes from the priced coronary findings alone.
hypotheses.criteria_block: none declared — the hypothesis is carried by the board alone

hypotheses.label: Another cause, unspecified (the residual share)

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. The residual bucket is kept large on purpose: pericarditis, musculoskeletal pain, biliary pain and the rest of the chest-pain differential live here unnamed, and the case's priced evidence has to beat an honest fifth of the board, not a token remainder.

hypotheses.mondo_note: No Mondo class is carried, by design: this hypothesis is a residual accounting bucket for the unnamed remainder of the differential, not a disease. Case #1's residual set the precedent — a bucket is not coded to a class it does not name.
hypotheses.criterion: Retired by exhaustion of the account: the coronary evidence chain (priced findings, the troponin rise, the angiogram) explains the whole presentation, and the bucket's share falls with the board's arithmetic to 0.0033 by stage 2.
hypotheses.criteria_block: none declared — the residual share is carried by the board alone

findings.text: 58 years old (case data). Age prices nothing on this board directly; it prices the HEART block's age item (45-65 years, 1 point, C72) — read off the chart by the block's own atom, not asserted by the narrative.

Six weeks ago this man attended this same department with the same central chest pain, and the workup was real: serial cardiac troponins negative, the resting ECG normal, and an exercise stress test negative for ischemia. He was discharged with the diagnosis 'non-cardiac chest pain, likely gastro-oesophageal reflux' and has taken omeprazole since (case data — the discharge summary is in his chart and the learner reads it). This finding is the case's anchoring exhibit, and its exact logical shape is the case: every element of it is TRUE — of that episode. A negative workup excludes an event at a time and a mechanism under test conditions: no necrosis then; no flow-limiting stenosis at stress then. It does not exclude a plaque that had not yet ruptured, in a man, for the future. The evidence the frame rests on is also asymmetric in the consulted literature: the Rational Clinical Examination prices a prior ABNORMAL stress test at LR 3.1 for ACS (C71) — it offers no ratio for a prior normal one, and this finding accordingly carries NO likelihood ratio in either direction. The board may not spend it; only the learner does.

The pain radiates to BOTH arms (case data). The Rational Clinical Examination prices radiation to both arms at LR 2.6 (95% CI 1.8-3.7; specificity 96%) for acute coronary syndrome (C71); the ratio is registered against the ACS hypothesis in the positive direction.

lr.note: LR+ 2.6 for ACS, cited from the Rational Clinical Examination (C71). Derivation in cases/parameters.json.

findings.text: The pain began at rest, about three hours before arrival, and is ongoing (case data). Rest onset and prolonged duration are among the specific elements by which Six's method classifies a history (C72); they carry no ratio of their own in this case — their price is paid inside the HEART block's history item, and the case does not charge them twice.

He is sweating through his shirt at rest in a cool room (case data). A specific element in Six's history classification (C72); no standalone ratio is registered for it — the consulted review prices the ECG and the radiation, not the sweat, and the case does not invent one.
Nauseated since the pain began; has felt sick twice, not vomited (case data). Carried as presentation evidence and a ground-truth phenotype term; no ratio is registered for it.

HEART history item, classified by Six's method (C72): the narrative contains primarily SPECIFIC elements — central pressure pain, at rest, prolonged, radiating to both arms, with diaphoresis and nausea — and no nonspecific pattern. Highly suspicious: 2 points.
HEART history item (C72): the mixed classification — some specific, some nonspecific elements — does not hold; the specific elements dominate. Absent.

HEART history item (C72): the nonspecific classification does not hold. Absent — and its absence is worth recording, because 'slightly suspicious' is the classification the recurrence frame would have preferred.

The arrival 12-lead ECG shows 1.5 mm of horizontal ST-segment depression across V4 to V6, and it is NEW: the tracing of six weeks ago was normal (case data). The Rational Clinical Examination prices ST-segment depression at LR 5.3 (95% CI 2.1-8.6; specificity 95%) for acute coronary syndrome (C71); the ratio is registered against the ACS hypothesis in the positive direction. The same finding prices the HEART block's ECG item at its top tier (significant ST depression, 2 points, C72) — one finding, two instruments, each reading it for its own question.

lr.note: LR+ 5.3 for ACS, cited from the Rational Clinical Examination (C71). Derivation in cases/parameters.json.

findings.text: HEART ECG item (C72): repolarisation abnormality WITHOUT significant ST depression does not describe this tracing — the depression is the finding. Absent.
HEART ECG item (C72): today's ECG is not normal. Absent — and the contrast is the case in miniature: 'normal ECG' is a true sentence about six weeks ago that the frame keeps trying to spend today.

HEART risk-factor item (C72): exactly TWO of Six's counted risk factors are present — diagnosed hypertension (treated) and family history of coronary artery disease (father's myocardial infarction at 58). One or two risk factors: 1 point. The counting is Six's, and the near-misses do not count: he stopped smoking nine years ago (Six counts current smokers and cessation within one month only), his cholesterol has never been diagnosed as hypercholesterolaemia, he has no treated diabetes, and a BMI of 27 is not obesity (all case data).

HEART risk-factor item (C72): neither three-or-more counted factors nor any history of atherosclerotic disease — no prior myocardial infarction, revascularisation, stroke or peripheral arterial disease (case data). Absent.
HEART risk-factor item (C72): 'no risk factors known' does not hold — two are counted. Absent.

No tearing, ripping or migratory pain; the pain does not radiate to the back; pulses are symmetric (case data). The dissection hypothesis's discriminating shape is absent. No ratio is registered for it — the absence stands as authored narrative evidence, as the pneumonia absences do.
The pain is not pleuritic — it does not vary with breathing or posture — and there is no dyspnea (case data). The embolism hypothesis's characteristic pain shape is absent.
Afebrile at 36.8 C, with no cough and a clear chest on auscultation (case data). The pneumonia hypothesis's presenting shape is absent.

The first cardiac troponin I is 0.34 ng/mL — above the assay's 0.04 ng/mL threshold, at 8.5 times it. The meta-analysis of conventional troponin assays at presentation gives summary sensitivity 0.72 and specificity 0.95 for adjudicated acute MI (C74); the computed LR+ of 14.4 is registered against the ACS hypothesis. The same value prices the HEART block's troponin item at its top tier — above twice the normal limit, 2 points (C72) — completing the score at 8. One number, three readings: the board's ratio, the score's points, and (with the repeat) the definition's criterion. The case keeps the three apart on purpose.

lr.note: LR+ 14.4 for the ACS hypothesis, computed as sensitivity / (1 - specificity) = 0.72 / (1 - 0.95) from the conventional-assay summary pair in C74. Derivation in cases/parameters.json.

findings.text: Chest radiograph (available on the test menu from stage 1): no consolidation, no effusion, no pneumothorax (case data). Recorded as the pneumonia hypothesis's anatomical absence. The model learner never orders this test — his board has no use for it inside the recurrence frame — and the case records the menu item un-ordered rather than pretending the film was taken in the learner's pathway.

The repeat cardiac troponin I is 1.72 ng/mL — a five-fold rise from the first sample's 0.34. This is the Universal Definition's kinetic criterion (C75): a rise of troponin with at least one value above the 99th percentile upper reference limit, which — with ischemic symptoms and new ischemic ECG changes — is myocardial infarction, not merely injury. It carries NO likelihood ratio: the rise is not evidence FOR the diagnosis in the board's sense, it is a constituent OF the diagnosis under the definition, and pricing it as a ratio would charge the same fact twice. The troponin HEART item does not re-open for it either: the block prices the first (admission) troponin only, and the repeat never re-enters it.

Coronary angiography: a 90% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery with thrombus at the lesion; the remaining vessels show no flow-limiting disease (case data — an authored encounter). A drug-eluting stent is placed with a good angiographic result. The finding carries no likelihood ratio: it is direct inspection, the identification of a coronary thrombus being itself one of the Universal Definition's ischemic criteria (C75). It is also the finding that closes the anchor argument anatomically: the artery the frame described as cleared is seen, and it is not clear.

labs.analyte: Cardiac troponin I (first sample, at presentation)
labs.interpretation: Above the threshold: 0.34 ng/mL is 8.5 times the 0.04 positivity threshold of the HEART derivation assay (Access AccuTroponin I, C72), concordant with the 0-0.04 ng/mL reference interval carried by C77. Two points in the HEART block (above twice the normal limit, C72) and the numerator of the case's computed ratio (C74). Pain began about three hours before this sample — inside the window in which troponin has had time to rise (C77).

1.72 ng/mL: a rise of 5.06-fold from the first sample (1.72 / 0.34). The Universal Definition's rise pattern (C75), and the value that breaks the learner's stage-2 rationalisation — the repeat was ordered to watch the level fall. Recorded as course data; the HEART block prices the ADMISSION troponin only and does not re-open for it — the score's validated use is the presentation, and the case keeps that discipline rather than re-pricing a diagnosis the definition has already made.

measurements.name: Pulse at arrival
measurements.interpretation: A tachycardia by the ward's habits but not by any item in this case: the HEART block has no pulse item, and no ratio in this case prices it. Recorded because the learner's stage-2 rationalisation reaches for it ('demand') — the measurement exists so the argument can be examined, not endorsed.

measurements.name: Systolic BP at arrival
measurements.interpretation: Case data. No score item in this case prices blood pressure.

measurements.name: Oxygen saturation at arrival (air)
measurements.interpretation: No hypoxaemia: part of the embolism and pneumonia hypotheses' quiet stage-1 weather. No ratio prices it.

available_tests.name: Cardiac troponin I (first sample)
available_tests.note: The blood test the whole case turns on: completes the HEART block, prices the board's strongest ratio, and opens the Universal Definition's kinetic question. Resource figures are verify-flagged placeholders by the house rule.

available_tests.name: Chest radiograph
available_tests.note: On the menu from arrival; the model learner never orders it. Recorded so the pneumonia hypothesis's anatomical absence is a test result the pathway COULD have produced, not an assertion — the workbench's menu discipline is about what was available, and the debrief's order tally covers only what was ordered.

available_tests.name: Cardiac troponin I (repeat sample)
available_tests.note: Ordered by the learner to watch the level fall — the serial measurement the kinetics require (C77: troponin rises over hours, and a first result is retested). It comes back five times higher. The HEART block does not re-open for it: admission values only.

available_tests.name: Coronary angiography (with PCI as indicated)
available_tests.note: The definitive act of the case: finds the lesion, identifies the thrombus the Universal Definition names (C75), and treats it in the same session. Indicated on the guideline's high-risk pathway — new ischemic ECG changes, troponin-confirmed myocardial injury, and a high-risk decision-pathway score (C76) — which is the HEART block's own completed band. Resource figures are verify-flagged placeholders by the house rule.

criteria_blocks.label: HEART score
criteria_blocks.system: Six 2008 (C72): the admission risk score for emergency-department chest pain — History, ECG, Age, Risk factors, Troponin, each 0-2 — built from the PRESENTATION: the arrival history as classified by Six's method, the arrival ECG, the chart age, the counted risk factors, and the FIRST troponin. In this case it prices exactly those: the troponin item references the first sample only, and the repeat value at stage 3 never re-enters it — the score's validated question is the disposition at the door, and the case keeps that discipline rather than re-pricing a diagnosis later evidence makes by definition. A partial total, while any item is unmeasured, is a floor and not a reading: the stage-1 board shows it that way on purpose, because a partially-computed 6 quoted without its missing item is how the recurrence frame would read it — 'moderate, observe' — while the floor already excludes the discharge band and the one unmeasured item can only raise it. Outcome risks are carried in the bands from both consulted cohorts (C72's derivation risks; C73's prospective validation).

items.label: History (Six's classification of the narrative)
items.text: Primarily specific elements — central pressure at rest, prolonged, radiating to both arms, with diaphoresis and nausea: highly suspicious, 2 points (C72). The classification is made from the narrative by Six's stated method, not from the conclusion the narrative arrives wrapped in.

items.label: ECG at presentation
items.text: 1.5 mm of new horizontal ST depression, V4-V6: significant ST depression, 2 points (C72). New is the operative word — the normal tracing this item would have scored six weeks ago is a different patient's-chart entry, in the only sense that matters: a different episode.

items.label: Age
items.text: 58 years old: 1 point (C72 — 45 to 65 years; the 65-and-over tier is encoded as age above 64, the methods text's '65 years or older').

items.label: Risk factors (Six's counted list)

tiers.label: 3 or more risk factors, or history of atherosclerotic disease

items.text: Two counted factors — diagnosed hypertension; family history of coronary artery disease: 1 point (C72). The ex-smoker of nine years and the undiagnosed 'borderline' cholesterol are not counted, because Six's list does not count them; the block scores the list as published, not as gestured at.

items.label: Troponin I — FIRST sample only (admission value)

tiers.label: More than twice the normal limit
One to twice the normal limit
At or below the normal limit

items.text: The first troponin is 0.34 ng/mL against a 0.04 limit — 8.5 times it: 2 points (C72). The item reads lab.troponin-i-first and nothing else, at every stage: the stage-3 repeat of 1.72 does not re-enter it, because the score prices the admission. The instrument that completes at stage 2 is the instrument the disposition argument at stage 2 must answer.

bands.label: low risk
bands.text: HEART 0-3: in Six's derivation cohort a 2.5% endpoint risk, supporting immediate discharge (C72); in Backus's prospective validation, a 1.7% six-week MACE rate (C73). The Rational Clinical Examination prices this band at LR 0.20 for ACS (C71). Nothing in this case comes near it: the stage-1 PARTIAL total of 6 already excludes it, before the troponin is even back.

bands.label: moderate risk
bands.text: HEART 4-6: a 20.3% endpoint risk in the derivation cohort — admission for clinical observation (C72); a 16.6% six-week MACE rate in the validation cohort (C73). While any item is unmeasured this total is a floor, not a reading: the one item unmeasured at stage 1 carries up to 2 of the scale's 10 points. His stage-1 partial total is 6 — the top of this band, with the troponin outstanding and able only to raise it.

bands.label: high risk
bands.text: HEART 7-10: a 72.7% endpoint risk in the derivation cohort, supporting early invasive strategies (C72); a 50.1% six-week MACE rate in the validation cohort (C73); the Rational Clinical Examination prices the band at LR 13 for ACS (C71). His completed score is 8: the band the disposition argument happens in, from stage 2 onward, whatever the recurrence frame says.

adjudication.diagnosis_label: Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction, type 1 (acute coronary syndrome): plaque disruption with thrombus, proximal left anterior descending artery

heart_score.reading: HEART 8 — the high band in both consulted cohorts: Six's derivation risk 72.7% for the combined endpoint, supporting early invasive strategies (C72); Backus's validation MACE rate 50.1% at six weeks (C73). The score completed at stage 2 on the first troponin and never re-priced.
heart_score.composition: History highly suspicious (2) + ECG significant ST depression (2) + age 58 (1) + two counted risk factors (1) + first troponin 0.34 ng/mL, 8.5 times the limit (2). The stage-1 partial was 6 — a floor that already excluded discharge — and the only direction the missing item could move it was up.

criteria_comparison.board_final_leader: hyp.acs-nstemi at 0.9884 on the workbench board from stage 2 onward — carried by the three priced findings (radiation 2.6, ST depression 5.3, troponin 14.4, C71/C74); the definition and the angiogram then settle what boards cannot: the diagnosis, and the lesion, seen.
criteria_comparison.anchor_retired_by: Anatomy: the angiogram shows a 90% proximal LAD stenosis with thrombus — the artery the recurrence frame described as cleared — after the arithmetic had already ruled the frame out at stage 2 (0.0043) on the first troponin. The prior workup is not retired and never needed to be: it remains a true finding about six weeks ago, which is all it ever was.
criteria_comparison.note: No score in this case diagnoses anything: the HEART block prices the admission disposition, the board prices the differential, and the Universal Definition (C75) — rise, ischemic symptoms, new ischemic ECG changes, thrombus at angiography — makes the diagnosis. The case keeps the three instruments separate on purpose, because the frame's whole strength was blurring them: it quoted a disposition-grade conclusion ('non-cardiac, discharge') as if it were a diagnosis-grade fact about the man.

excluded.basis: Ruled out arithmetically at stage 2 (0.0043) by the first troponin — evidence the frame cannot absorb without ceasing to be itself — then retired anatomically at angiography. As a bare word it names a real disease he may also have; as the frame used it — the same pain, already excluded, safe to send home — it is the case's refuted claim. The workup it rests on is NOT refuted: negative troponins, a normal tracing and a negative stress test were true findings about that episode, and the case's discipline is to say exactly what they were findings about.

Carried below the rule-out threshold at stage 1 (0.0165) by the priced coronary evidence; the pain is not pleuritic and there is no dyspnea or hypoxaemia. No embolism imaging is claimed: the exclusion is arithmetical and clinical, completed by the angiogram's full coronary account. Recorded honestly — troponin elevation is compatible with embolism (C77), which is why this hypothesis is excluded by the whole picture and not by the troponin.

Below the rule-out threshold at stage 1 (0.0083); no tearing or migratory pain, no pulse deficit, and the presentation assembles completely into the coronary account. No aortic imaging is claimed or fabricated.

Ruled out at stage 2 (0.0020). Afebrile, no cough, clear chest, and a radiograph on the menu that shows no consolidation — the hypothesis falls on absences the case declines to price with ratios it does not have.
The residual share falls to 0.0033 by stage 2 as the priced evidence accumulates on the truth; nothing in the course suggests a named alternative the bucket was sheltering.

adjudication.note: Ground truth is the angiogram and the definition together: a rise of troponin from 0.34 to 1.72 ng/mL with ischemic symptoms and new ischemic ECG changes satisfies the Fourth Universal Definition (C75), and the angiogram identifies the type 1 mechanism — plaque disruption with thrombus in the proximal LAD. The adjudication's discipline is the case's: the scores price disposition and differential, the definition diagnoses, and the prior workup is honoured for exactly what it was — a competent, negative evaluation of a different episode, whose only false note was struck by everyone who later quoted it as a verdict on the man.

ground_truth.diagnosis: Type 1 non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction: atherosclerotic plaque disruption with thrombus, 90% proximal left anterior descending stenosis, treated with a drug-eluting stent. Troponin I 0.34 ng/mL on arrival rising to 1.72; HEART score 8 on admission values (partial 6 at stage 1). The prior episode's negative workup was genuine and is not revised: it evaluated an episode six weeks earlier and found no infarction and no flow-limiting disease — it was never capable of excluding the plaque that had not yet ruptured.

management.disposition: Admit to a monitored coronary-care bed under cardiology. The completed HEART score of 8 (C72) places him in the band both consulted cohorts price as high-risk (C72: 72.7% endpoint risk; C73: 50.1% six-week MACE), and the disposition the score supports — and the guideline's high-risk pathway requires (C76) — is the early invasive one he received. Discharge, the disposition the recurrence frame was arguing for, is refused in the alternatives below.
management.antithrombotic_therapy: Antiplatelet and anticoagulant therapy for non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome per the consulted chest-pain guideline's high-risk pathway (C76): aspirin promptly, with further antiplatelet and anticoagulant agents per the treating team's protocol around the invasive strategy. This record names the strategy and its source; it does not fix doses, because no consulted source in this milestone fixes them and the precision discipline of this module does not borrow them from memory.
management.invasive_strategy: Coronary angiography with percutaneous intervention as indicated — performed: 90% proximal LAD stenosis with thrombus, drug-eluting stent placed, good result. The indication is the guideline's high-risk triad as this case assembles it (C76): new ischemic ECG changes, troponin-confirmed myocardial injury, and a high-risk decision-pathway score — the HEART block's own completed 8.
management.secondary_prevention: The conversation and the chart both change after this admission: the discharge diagnosis of six weeks ago is annotated in the record as superseded — not wrong about its episode, but closed — so that the NEXT presentation does not inherit it as a premise; lipid management and risk-factor review are arranged against his two counted factors and the ones the score did not count (his smoking stopped nine years ago and stays stopped). The omeprazole continues on its own merits; it was never the treatment for this.

alternatives_considered.option: Discharge with reassurance — 'the same pain as six weeks ago, already worked up and excluded'
alternatives_considered.verdict: REFUSED: a completed HEART score of 8 (C72/C73), a new ST-depression the earlier tracing did not have, and a troponin 8.5 times the limit. This alternative is the anchoring event wearing a disposition's clothes: it quotes a true negative workup about a past episode as a verdict on a present one. The case exists so the workbench can watch it be refused on numbers, not on seniority.

alternatives_considered.option: Repeat the exercise stress test — re-run the test that was negative, rather than angiography
alternatives_considered.verdict: REFUSED: the presentation has already crossed the line a functional test exists to interrogate. With troponin-confirmed myocardial injury and new ischemic ECG changes, the consulted guideline's pathway is invasive coronary angiography (C76); a stress test re-asks, at a week's delay and some risk, the one question the troponin kinetics have already answered — and its six-week-old negative twin is the premise this case is about.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat as reflux: continue omeprazole, antacids, observe the pain settle
alternatives_considered.verdict: REFUSED: this is the anchor as a prescription. The pain 'settling' is compatible with a completed infarction; the settling of the prior episodes is part of how an unscoped ulcer — and an unruptured plaque — tell their stories. Nothing in the consulted evidence prices a proton-pump inhibitor against a troponin of 1.72 ng/mL.

validity.internal_structure: Every quantitative clinical assertion traces to the register: the two history/ECG likelihood ratios to the Rational Clinical Examination (C71), cited as published; the troponin ratio to the conventional-assay meta-analysis (C74), computed from its summary sensitivity and specificity with the derivation in the register; the HEART block's items, bands and disposition actions to its derivation paper (C72), with its outcome risks seconded by the prospective validation (C73); the diagnostic criteria to the Fourth Universal Definition (C75); the high-risk pathway and the angiography indication to the 2021 chest-pain guideline (C76), consulted through its official slide set and pocket guide; the troponin kinetics and the non-MI causes of elevation to MedlinePlus (C77). The ontology identifiers were resolved against EBI OLS in-session, including two recorded refusals (the dissection hypothesis's Mondo; the unreturned NSTEMI class). The workbench recomputes every stage board from priors and ratios alone, classifies every model-learner order from the revealed evidence, and evaluates the declared block mechanically; the anchoring tally is computed, not asserted. Two scope notes are carried on the record rather than smoothed: the troponin ratio's source target is adjudicated MI, applied here to the ACS hypothesis; and the case's assay is the conventional one the HEART item was defined on, against the current guideline's high-sensitivity preference (C76) — the substitution the literature has made is recorded, and the case's internal consistency is kept instead of an anachronism in either direction.
validity.consequences: Formative use only: the case teaches a reasoning failure — the conversion of an episode-indexed negative workup into a patient-indexed immunity — and its scores (the HEART block, the boards, the Brier tallies) are instruments for that teaching, not assessments of any clinician and not guidance for any real patient.
